tasks.short: Define project staffing needs, assess candidates and coordinate hiring.

steps.what: Agree required skills, responsibilities, start dates and contract duration.
Approve headcount, funding and recruitment route.
Create and publish the vacancy from the approved staffing request.
Review applications and agree an interview shortlist.
Interview shortlisted candidates and discuss relevant project experience.
Choose a candidate and approve proposed employment terms.
Generate and issue the offer using approved terms.
Request onboarding after receiving candidate acceptance.

tasks.design: Configure approved role and offer templates, recruitment stages and release approvals in the {ATS}. A flow in the {WORKFLOW} checks staffing approval against the {ERP} budget and creates an onboarding request in the {HCM} after recorded acceptance. People define requirements, assess suitability, interview and make hiring decisions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Staffing approval, candidate records and onboarding were separate. Teams also needed agreement on reusable role templates and hiring authority.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing configuration handles much of the flow. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of connecting approval and appointment records.
tasks.still_hard: Assessing suitability and persuading candidates remain human work. GDPR, employment requirements and national rules affect access and retention; introducing AI candidate evaluation would require a separate EU AI Act assessment.
tasks.human_edge: Understand the project's real skill gaps, judge relevant experience fairly and build candidate trust.

ambition.what: Weekly internal redeployment review while critical project vacancies remain open.

tasks.altitude: The project manager spends less time chasing approvals and repeating staffing details. They can compare redeployment and recruitment options more often; hiring and budget rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Coordinate workplace readiness for confirmed project starters.
reach.learn: Learn equipment lead times, access requirements and starter readiness checks.

evidence.claim: Recruitment configuration and deterministic handoffs can reduce administration without automating candidate suitability decisions.
Textkernel documents CV parsing and matching. This supports parsing feasibility, not autonomous hiring or this design's savings.
Step shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured customer outcomes.

assumptions: The project manager contributes as hiring manager; a recruiter administers recruitment.
The target uses approved templates and explicit criteria without model-based candidate ranking.
Build ranges cover one staffing workflow; access and employee consultation under national rules may extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Which recruitment, finance and employee-record interfaces are available?
Who may approve headcount, shortlist decisions and employment terms?
Which templates, retention periods and national consultation requirements apply?
research_questions: Can existing recruitment configuration handle approvals and accepted-offer events?
How much delay comes from approval waiting rather than active administration?
Would any proposed screening feature evaluate candidates through AI?
new_work: Maintain approved role, offer and onboarding templates.
Resolve mismatched budget references and failed onboarding handoffs.
Review recruitment access and retention settings.

tasks.short: Review project contributions, discuss performance and agree support or improvement actions.

steps.what: Review assigned work, deliverables and recorded project commitments.
Ask the team member about blockers, workload and missing context.
Assess contribution against agreed expectations and relevant context.
Prepare specific feedback examples and proposed support actions.
Give feedback, hear the response and agree practical support actions.
Record agreed actions, employee response and the next review date.

tasks.design: Configure a restricted view in the {PROJECT} that brings together agreed commitments and accepted deliverables. Templates in the {DOCS} assemble source-linked examples and the manager's own assessment; the {TALENT} records approved actions and review dates. The solution produces no worker score or model-written performance judgement.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence was scattered, while project records lacked the context needed for fair feedback. Managers could not safely equate task activity with contribution.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured views and forms can assemble existing evidence and reduce repeated entry. Small integrations are cheaper to build, without requiring a model to evaluate employees.
tasks.still_hard: Fair assessment needs context about dependencies, role expectations and support. GDPR and national rules govern employee data and consultation; AI worker evaluation would require a separate EU AI Act assessment.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish a capability issue from poor conditions, deliver difficult feedback and agree credible support.

ambition.what: Fortnightly adjustment of agreed support actions during difficult project phases.

tasks.altitude: The project manager spends less preparation time collecting examples and more time understanding obstacles. Formal appraisal, pay and disciplinary authority remain with their existing owners.

reach.task: Investigate recurring process barriers behind missed project commitments.
reach.learn: Learn process mapping, dependency analysis and how to separate system problems from individual contribution.

evidence.claim: Existing project views, feedback templates and action records can reduce preparation without automating performance judgement.
Task counts and completion times alone are insufficient evidence of individual performance.
Step shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates; the digest contains no matching deployment case.

assumptions: Feedback concerns project contribution rather than a formal disciplinary process.
The target reuses disclosed work records and introduces no message surveillance or inferred employee scores.
The access range includes privacy review and employee consultation under applicable national rules; formal processes may take longer.
unknowns: Which project evidence may managers access and retain for feedback?
Does the project manager have permission to write feedback records?
Which employee consultation, representation and correction procedures apply?
Are existing project records sufficiently complete and contextual?
research_questions: Can restricted views expose relevant evidence without disclosing unrelated employee information?
Does template preparation save meaningful time once context gathering is preserved?
Would any planned feature cross from factual retrieval into AI worker evaluation?
new_work: Correct misleading or incomplete contribution records.
Maintain access restrictions and retention settings.
Review generated evidence packs before feedback discussions.
Follow up support actions and record employee corrections.

tasks.short: Develop and maintain an approved project plan covering scope, schedule, funding, technology and staffing.

steps.what: Read the brief, commitments and constraints before planning.

loop.input: Approved project brief, client commitments and technical constraints.
loop.output: Structured objectives, requirements, constraints and unresolved questions with source references.
loop.check: Validate required fields and source references; the project manager confirms interpretations and conflicts.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per document batch; unresolved conflicts return to the project manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative briefs express commitments and constraints inconsistently; fixed field mappings miss their meaning.

steps.what: Agree scope, delivery approach, technical choices and acceptance criteria.
Build activities, dependencies, milestones and a feasible delivery schedule.
Calculate staffing, procurement costs, funding needs and contingency.
Assemble the plan, assumptions, risks and responsibilities.
Review trade-offs and approve the project baseline.
Publish the approved baseline and notify delivery owners.

tasks.design: A bounded extraction loop turns approved material in the {DOCS} into source-linked planning inputs. Configure dependency scheduling in the {PROJECT}; deterministic calculations combine accepted estimates with rates from the {ERP} and capacity from the {HCM}, then generate a versioned plan in the {DOCS}. Approval in the {WORKFLOW} permits baseline publication and owner notifications.
tasks.previous_blocker: Narrative requirements, resource assumptions and cost calculations lived separately. Plan changes required repeated copying and reconciliation across documents and schedules.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded extraction can prepare inconsistent briefs for review. AI-assisted coding reduces the cost of calculation, validation and document-generation glue; scheduling still uses established algorithms.
tasks.still_hard: People must supply credible estimates and resolve technical, staffing and funding trade-offs. Deterministic schedules can appear precise despite uncertain assumptions.
tasks.human_edge: Choose a workable delivery approach, challenge optimistic estimates and secure real resource commitments.

ambition.what: Weekly selection between recovery schedules within the approved scope and funding envelope.

tasks.altitude: The project manager spends more time testing alternatives with delivery leads and less time rebuilding plans. They gain faster choices within existing tolerances; scope, funding and baseline approval rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Identify material and production constraints affecting project milestones.
reach.learn: Learn lead-time variability, capacity calendars and dependency escalation.

reach.task: Plan technical dependencies, testing windows and release readiness.
reach.learn: Learn technical estimation uncertainty and release acceptance requirements.

evidence.claim: Dependency scheduling, cost calculations and template generation are established deterministic techniques.
A bounded extraction loop can prepare narrative planning inputs, subject to source and interpretation checks.
The digest provides no direct project-planning deployment case; time and build estimates remain unvalidated.

assumptions: Delivery leads provide effort estimates and technical choices; the model does not invent them.
One project type and one approval route are included in the initial build.
Only necessary capacity data is exposed; employee consultation under national rules may extend the access range.
Plan updates use the same preparation flow; baseline changes follow approval tolerances.
unknowns: Which scheduling and resource features are already configured?
Are rates, working calendars and capacity records reliable and accessible?
Who approves baselines and changes at each tolerance?
Which document formats, languages and technical constraints must be supported?
research_questions: Can existing scheduling configuration meet the required capacity constraints?
Which requirements need interpretation rather than direct field mapping?
How well do generated schedules reproduce accepted historical plans using the same inputs?
Which cost and capacity connectors justify their maintenance cost?
new_work: Review extracted commitments and resolve conflicting requirements.
Maintain rate mappings, planning templates and working calendars.
Investigate infeasible schedules and missing resource commitments.
Check baseline versions and approval references.

tasks.short: Assemble reliable project status and explain exceptions and required decisions to managers.

steps.what: Collect delivery updates, technical issues and customer feedback from workstream leads.

loop.input: Submitted workstream updates and authorised customer feedback for the reporting period.
loop.output: Source-linked progress, blockers, customer concerns and missing responses.
loop.check: Validate project, reporting period and source references; retain conflicting updates as exceptions.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per reporting batch; unresolved items go to the project manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Technical issues and customer concerns arrive as varied free text. Structured submission fields should replace extraction where practical.

steps.what: Read schedule progress, recorded costs, commitments and resource availability.
Reconcile cut-offs and calculate budget, milestone and capacity variances.
Draft the status report with causes, risks and requested decisions.

loop.input: Validated metrics, source-linked updates, risk register and approved report structure.
loop.output: Draft exception narrative with source references and explicit unknowns.
loop.check: Insert numbers deterministically; verify factual claims against sources and prohibit unsupported causal explanations.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass per report; unsupported sections become questions for the project manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cover metrics, but combining varied issue narratives into a concise explanation requires language synthesis.

steps.what: Validate material exceptions and decide which issues require management attention.
Send the status report to authorised managers.
Explain significant issues, answer challenges and agree management actions.

tasks.design: Scheduled jobs on the {DATA_PLATFORM} reconcile project identifiers, cut-offs and metrics from the {PROJECT}, {ERP} and permitted {HCM} capacity data into the {BI}. Bounded loops extract submitted updates and draft source-linked exception commentary in the {DOCS}, while all numerical calculations remain deterministic. A release approval in the {WORKFLOW} distributes the report through the {EMAIL} and records its version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Project and finance records used different identifiers and reporting cut-offs. Narrative updates still required chasing, interpreting and copying into management reports.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable connectors and cheaper integration development make reconciliation practical. Small bounded loops can handle narrative updates while calculations and publication remain controlled.
tasks.still_hard: Late costs, optimistic updates and inconsistent customer feedback can undermine accuracy. People must distinguish symptoms from causes and decide when escalation helps.
tasks.human_edge: Explain uncertainty candidly, challenge reassuring accounts and secure specific management decisions.

ambition.what: A mid-cycle sponsor briefing when a milestone or funding tolerance is breached.

tasks.altitude: The project manager spends less time assembling reports and more time resolving exceptions with managers. They can initiate earlier escalation, while funding and scope decisions retain their existing approvers.

reach.task: Compare recurring causes of project delay across the portfolio.
reach.learn: Learn comparable metric definitions, cause coding and the limits of cross-project comparisons.

reach.task: Identify project disruptions that threaten critical operational dependencies.
reach.learn: Learn impact thresholds, dependency mapping and continuity escalation routes.

evidence.claim: Reconciliation, variance calculations, dashboards and scheduled report distribution are established deterministic patterns.
The digest documents a report containing nonexistent sources, supporting explicit source validation for generated commentary.
The digest contains no project-status automation case establishing these savings; time and build ranges are estimates.

assumptions: The report is for internal managers; external client publication would need a separate release action and authority.
The initial build covers one report format and a limited set of project and finance sources.
Only required staffing capacity is used; GDPR controls and national employee consultation requirements apply where relevant.
Passive mailbox reading can be replaced progressively with structured workstream submissions.
unknowns: Are project identifiers consistent across schedule, finance and staffing records?
How are accruals, commitments, forecasts and reporting cut-offs defined?
Which managers may see financial, customer and staffing details?
Who approves report release and owns escalation thresholds?
research_questions: Can existing reporting configuration replace any proposed custom connector?
Which report sections genuinely require prose rather than metric templates?
How often do late transactions materially change an issued report?
Can historical reports establish useful reconciliation and unsupported-claim checks?
new_work: Resolve missing updates, stale data and unmatched project references.
Maintain metric definitions, cut-off rules and recipient permissions.
Review generated commentary and approve report release.
Monitor connector failures and changes to source fields.
Tune exception thresholds when alerts prove unhelpful.

role.altitude: The project manager's week shifts toward delivery choices, staffing conversations and resolving exceptions. Preparation becomes faster, while hiring, employee assessment, funding and scope authority stay with their existing decision makers.
reach: Administrative services managers: coordinate readiness for confirmed project starters.
Management analysts: investigate recurring delivery barriers and portfolio patterns.
Information technology project managers: connect technical dependencies to delivery plans.
Business continuity planners: connect project disruptions to critical operations.
skills_to_grow: Define consistent project, cost and capacity data.
Test schedules and budgets against uncertain assumptions.
Review source-linked extraction and generated commentary.
Give fair feedback using evidence and context.
Learn access, privacy and national employee consultation requirements.
role.ambitious_version: Provide a recurring project decision service: compare recovery options, surface staffing gaps and bring sponsors specific choices before tolerances are breached. Earn any wider decision rights through explicit delegation and demonstrated delivery judgement.
